falseClaims: The high rollback finding claims other readers can see partially written rows from a transaction that later aborts. refresh wraps all inserts and activation in db.transaction; PostgreSQL does not expose these dirty reads, even at its Read Uncommitted setting.

The null/undefined finding says the expression relies on loose equality. It actually uses strict === after explicitly normalizing undefined with ?? null, which is exactly why headline NULL rows match correctly.

The raw-type finding presents bigint-as-string as a NaN mechanism for Number(). Numeric bigint strings convert successfully; the aggregate count is explicitly cast to PostgreSQL integer. No invalid adapter value or unsafe count is demonstrated.

independent:moonshotai/kimi-k2.5:pr376:3.notes: Frozen trends service:410-416 starts one transaction and an advisory transaction lock; :615-624 calls the hook then swaps active generations inside it. PostgreSQL transaction-isolation documentation explicitly excludes dirty reads: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/transaction-iso.html . The caller can perform separate reads straddling a successful commit under Read Committed, but that is not the claimed visibility of a rolled-back transaction. FK RESTRICT truly prevents deleting currently referenced material/specific rows; that is an integrity policy, not proof the schema should cascade-delete published aggregates. Expression-index filtering concerns are hypothetical: the actual collection read filters by generation_id (the index's leading ordinary column) and filters material in the UI; no server material-query execution plan is supplied. Dedicated invalid-scope/RESTRICT tests are absent from the new integration test; lack of them does not mean valid rows bypass the constraints. Count conversion source uses count(distinct ...)::integer. ER reverses cardinalities, implying at most one trend row references each material/product type/specific, though many generations/scopes may reference them. Generated snapshot omission is disclosed and exact catalog/privacy-safe collection distinction is retained.

Suppressing the hidden row thus cannot uniquely cause a false notice; removing it before the threshold comparison leaves the real general-bucket suppression. getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends runs its own SQL at service:128-208, independently of refresh, so it needs a separate change to remove analogous response rows. Default populated headline/materialSpecificId search states and >8-material Other overflow lack dedicated new fixtures; the test gap is source-supported, although the illustrative 'drop a predicate and empty charts' wording is not a demonstrated regression. The repeated eleven-detail UNION scan and duplicate object mapping are true static cost/maintainability observations, not measured performance defects. The focused ER correctly shows global material_specific.id PK, many-to-one nullable trend dimensions, generation required, and a specific's required parent material. Exact catalog, privacy threshold, rounding, transaction swap and omission disclosures are accurate. No high/critical blocker.
